exposure: Labor followed by intrapartum cesarean delivery (IN-CD)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 13,686,776 low-risk individuals with singleton, nonanomalous pregnancies delivered at 37 to 41 weeks in the U.S. between 2016 and 2021.
finding: Among low-risk pregnancies, attempting labor was associated with a lower risk of composite adverse outcomes compared to planned cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Compared to planned cesarean delivery, the risk of adverse outcomes was lower with vaginal delivery after labor, but higher with intrapartum cesarean delivery after labor.
followup_time: N/A (infant death implies up to 1 year, but a specific overall follow-up time for all outcomes is not mentioned)
